I roasted a whole chicken last night and thought I'd make the leftovers into a chicken salad. Does anyone have any good recipes or tips? I've never made a chicken salad. I roasted the chicken with preserved lemons, so it has a definite lemon-y taste to it, if that matters.

When I make chicken salad with leftovers I usually don't follow a recipe, don't follow them in general really. I like to see what I have available and go with it. Base of chicken, mayo, S & P and the rest is up to you. You could put a little thyme to compliment the lemon-y taste and maybe add a little finely chopped or grated onion. Some celery, whatever looks good. You might just make something delicious!! If you're worried about wasting food just mix up really small amounts together to taste and then you can do the rest if you like it. I use this technique almost every time I cook. It makes cooking fun and exciting to me.

Wow, I love throwing roasted chicken on ANY salad.

I usually just half fill a bowl with spinach or chopped kale (or romaine, really, whatever greens I have in my fridge). Then I pile on my favorite veggies - red peppers, green onions, mushrooms, chopped tomatoes, avocado). Shred the chicken on top of that. Then grab a good lemon vinaigrette, or make a quick one, and sprinkle on.

Make it easy on yourself! Use what is already in your fridge, if you can.

Example vinaigrette recipe (via food.com):

  • 1⁄4 cup fresh lemon juice
  • 1 teaspoon lemon zest
  • 2 tablespoons white wine vinegar
  • 1⁄4 teaspoon salt
  • 1⁄4 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 tablespoon sugar
  • 1⁄4 cup finely grated parmesan cheese
  • 1⁄4 cup extra virgin olive oil

Whisk everything but the oil together, and then slowly drizzle the oil in (a.k.a - emulse it!). Drizzle on salad and viola! Eat.

1. Probably Beserk, the very detailed and dark setting made for some really good artwork and it's probably one of the best reasons to read it.

I don't have an overall favorite style, but I tend toward things that are unusual and well-done. The normal, garish, highly detailed and stylized look of the things that most consider to be the best leaves me sort of cold. I admire the skill it requires, but it just doesn't impress me that much. I'm more impressed by artists who have a unique style that works well. The two best examples I can think of for that are Dowman Seiman and Kusano Kouichi (Onisuki). The latter is probably my favorite example of the sort of thing that impresses me, since his art style is completely unlike anything anyone else does, and it's very well executed and works well in the context of the series. But it's not at all the sort of thing that most people think of as great art style.

Probably the closest I come to overlapping with the standard conception of good art is with Mori Kaoru (Otoyomegatari), and that shouldn't really be surprising, since she's arguably the best artist working in manga right now.

The only time I remember even considering stopping reading a manga because of the art style was with EArTh, and that was because the mangaka drew such dense and complex images that it was often tough to sort out what was actually happening, and that was paired with a dense and complex plot that also made it tough to sort out what was actually happening. But I liked it enough that I struggled through anyway. I can't even imagine being offended or disturbed by an art style enough to not read something.
